name: JGWS Media Optimizer
author: jgwebstudio

sections.description:
Automatic JPG/JPEG to WebP Conversion for WordPress

Convert JPG and JPEG images to WebP automatically – directly on your WordPress site.

JGWS Media Optimizer is a lightweight WordPress plugin that automatically converts newly uploaded JPG and JPEG images to WebP during the normal WordPress Media Library upload process.

No extra steps are required. Upload your images and let the plugin handle the conversion.

Local image processing – no external optimization service required.

Image conversion takes place directly on your WordPress server using WordPress native image processing mechanisms. Your images do not need to be sent to an external image optimization service or API.

There are no conversion credits, monthly conversion quotas or per-image conversion fees. Actual processing performance depends on your hosting environment and available server resources.

Why use JGWS Media Optimizer?

Automatic JPG/JPEG to WebP conversion

Newly uploaded JPG and JPEG images are automatically converted to WebP as part of the normal WordPress Media Library workflow.

Local processing – no external image optimization service

Images are processed locally on your WordPress server. No external image optimization service or API is required for JPG/JPEG to WebP conversion.

No conversion credits or monthly quotas

There are no conversion credits, monthly conversion quotas or per-image conversion charges.

Keep a scaled JPG/JPEG copy

You can choose to keep a JPG/JPEG copy as a separate attachment in the WordPress Media Library. The kept copy is scaled down to the maximum size (2560 px by default), so the full-size original does not take up disk space.

By default, the JPG/JPEG file is removed after a successful conversion.

Clear image format labels in the Media Library

The plugin displays visible format labels to help you identify image files in the WordPress Media Library.

Supported format labels include JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, SVG, GIF, BMP and TIFF.

These labels make it easier to recognize image formats and identify files converted to WebP.

WordPress image sizes and imported images

JGWS Media Optimizer also generates WebP versions for image sizes created by WordPress during its normal image processing workflow.

The plugin can process supported images added through compatible external image import and content-creation mechanisms. It has been tested with images imported from Pexels through Kadence templates.

Features

  • Automatic conversion of newly uploaded JPG and JPEG images to WebP.
  • Conversion during the normal WordPress Media Library upload workflow.
  • Local image processing using WordPress native image processing mechanisms.
  • No external image optimization service or API required for JPG/JPEG to WebP conversion.
  • No conversion credits, monthly conversion quotas or per-image conversion fees.
  • Optional scaled JPG/JPEG copy kept as a separate Media Library attachment.
  • Visible format labels for JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, SVG, GIF, BMP and TIFF files.
  • WebP versions generated for WordPress-created image sizes.
  • Compatibility with supported external image import mechanisms and dynamically loaded Media Library content.
  • Default WebP quality of 85.
  • PDF preview images generated by WordPress are not converted to WebP.

JGWS Media Optimizer PRO

Need more control over image formats and quality – or want to convert the images you already have?

JGWS Media Optimizer PRO extends the FREE version with more output formats, full quality control and a safe bulk conversion of your existing Media Library.

NEW in PRO 2.2: Bulk conversion of your existing Media Library

Convert the images already stored on your site to WebP or AVIF in a few guided steps, with checks before anything is changed:

  1. Server check – confirms that your server can convert images.
  2. Analysis – scans your Media Library and shows what can be converted and how much disk space you can save.
  3. Simulation – tests a sample, so you can see the result before the real conversion.
  4. Conversion – converts images in small batches, with visible progress.
  5. URL replacement – updates image addresses on your site so they point to the new files.
  6. Freeing disk space – moves the old JPG and PNG files to quarantine first, so you can restore them. Delete them for good only when you are sure. Optional 301 redirects from the old addresses.

Everything runs on your own server, with no external service, no credits and no limits.

PRO also lets you:

  • Choose WebP or AVIF as the output format.
  • Configure WebP and AVIF quality from 1 to 100.
  • Convert new PNG images to WebP or AVIF.
  • Use separate conversion settings for JPG/JPEG and PNG.
  • Convert PNG images to WebP in lossless mode.
  • Keep a scaled JPG/JPEG or PNG copy of your uploads, so the large originals do not fill your disk.
  • Turn the conversion of JPG/JPEG and PNG on or off separately.

Learn more about JGWS Media Optimizer PRO →

FREE and PRO

The FREE version provides automatic JPG/JPEG to WebP conversion with a fixed WebP quality of 85, local image processing, an optional scaled JPG/JPEG copy and visible format labels for JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, SVG, GIF, BMP and TIFF files.

JGWS Media Optimizer PRO adds bulk conversion of existing images, more output formats, conversion quality control and PNG processing.

The PRO version includes:

  • Bulk conversion of your existing Media Library to WebP or AVIF, with analysis, simulation, quarantine and restore of old files, URL replacement and optional 301 redirects.
  • WebP and AVIF output format selection.
  • Configurable WebP and AVIF quality from 1 to 100.
  • PNG to WebP and AVIF conversion.
  • Separate conversion settings for JPG/JPEG and PNG.
  • Lossless PNG to WebP conversion.
  • Optional scaled copies of JPG/JPEG and PNG files.

For more information about the PRO version:

https://jgwebstudio.pl/en/wtyczki-wordpress/jgws-media-optimizer/#JGWS-Media-Optimizer-PRO

How It Works

When a JPG or JPEG image is added to the WordPress Media Library – through a standard upload or a compatible image import mechanism – JGWS Media Optimizer uses the WordPress image editor system to process the image and its registered sizes.

The uploaded JPG/JPEG image and its generated image sizes are converted to WebP using a fixed quality of 85.

WebP files are marked with a WEBP label in the Media Library. The plugin also displays format labels for JPG, PNG, AVIF, SVG, GIF, BMP and TIFF files.

By default, the JPG/JPEG file is removed after a successful conversion. If the option to keep a JPG/JPEG copy is enabled, the scaled-down JPG/JPEG file is kept as a separate attachment in the Media Library.

The kept copy is scaled down to the maximum size (2560 px by default). The full-size original is not kept, so it does not take up disk space.

Settings

The FREE version provides the following setting:

  • Keep a JPG/JPEG copy – keeps the scaled-down JPG/JPEG file as a separate Media Library attachment.

WebP quality is fixed at 85 in the FREE version.

External Services

This plugin uses Freemius (https://freemius.com/), a third-party service, for the plugin account, licensing, updates and the optional PRO version. Freemius, Inc. is the merchant of record for PRO purchases.

Freemius is contacted only after you choose to connect the plugin with a Freemius account on the opt-in screen, use the upgrade functionality, or activate a PRO license. Images, post content, Media Library files and plugin settings are never sent.

When connected, the Freemius SDK sends:

  • the address of your website and an anonymous installation ID,
  • the plugin version and the SDK version,
  • the state of the plugin (active, deactivated or uninstalled),
  • for a PRO license: the license key and the name and e-mail address of the license owner.

Optionally, if you allow it on the opt-in screen:

  • diagnostic information: WordPress and PHP versions, site language and site title,
  • the list of installed plugins and themes (names, versions and whether they are active).

If you deactivate the plugin, you may be asked for the reason, and the answer you choose is sent. The plugin also checks Freemius for updates.

Freemius Privacy Policy: https://freemius.com/privacy/

Freemius Terms of Service: https://freemius.com/terms/
sections.installation:
1. Upload the jgws-media-optimizer folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to the plugin settings and configure the available options.
  4. Upload JPG or JPEG images to the WordPress Media Library.

The plugin automatically processes newly uploaded JPG and JPEG images.
sections.faq:
Does the plugin convert JPG and JPEG images automatically?

Yes. Newly uploaded JPG and JPEG images are automatically converted to WebP.

Does the plugin convert existing images?

The FREE version processes newly uploaded JPG and JPEG images. It does not convert images that are already in your Media Library.

JGWS Media Optimizer PRO adds bulk conversion of your existing Media Library to WebP or AVIF. It works in guided steps: server check, analysis, simulation, conversion, URL replacement and freeing disk space.

Is the bulk conversion in PRO safe?

Yes. You can see the analysis and test a simulation before anything is converted. After the conversion, the old JPG and PNG files are first moved to quarantine, so you can restore them. They are deleted for good only when you decide so.

Can I keep a JPG/JPEG copy?

By default, the JPG/JPEG file is removed after a successful conversion. You can enable the option to keep a JPG/JPEG copy as a separate Media Library attachment.

Note: The kept copy is scaled down to the maximum size (2560 px by default). The full-size original is not kept, so it does not take up disk space.

Does the plugin require an external image optimization service?

No. JPG/JPEG to WebP conversion uses WordPress native image processing mechanisms and does not require an external image optimization service or API.

The plugin does use Freemius for account, licensing and related functionality. Usage tracking is optional and requires user consent.

Are there any conversion limits or credits?

No. The plugin does not use conversion credits, monthly conversion quotas or per-image conversion fees. Image processing takes place locally on your WordPress server. Actual processing performance depends on your hosting environment and available server resources.

What image quality does the FREE version use?

The FREE version uses a fixed WebP quality of 85. JGWS Media Optimizer PRO allows you to configure WebP and AVIF quality from 1 to 100, separately for JPG/JPEG and PNG.

Does the plugin convert PNG images or support AVIF conversion?

PNG conversion and AVIF output are available in JGWS Media Optimizer PRO.

Can I see which image formats are used?

Yes. The FREE version displays format labels for JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, SVG, GIF, BMP and TIFF files in the WordPress Media Library.

Does the plugin work with imported images?

JGWS Media Optimizer can process supported images added to the WordPress Media Library through compatible image import mechanisms.
